blocks.text: The full algorithm has two sequential costs: preprocessing and scanning. Their sum is O(n log n + n), which simplifies to O(n log n) because n log n grows faster than n. O(n) counts only the scan and omits sorting. O(1) and O(log n) are too small because even the scan may inspect a linear number of pairs. O(n^2) is an upper bound but not the tight bound: neither phase examines every pair. When the input is already sorted, or when one sort is amortized across many queries, the relevant cost model changes.
